 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Trilogy time … Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili is finally here!
 The bitter Bantamweight rivalry reaches its conclusion today (Sat., Oct. 24, 2026) inside Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, as the reigning and former champions collide for a third (and likely final) time at UFC 333 ( full results here ).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There is no shortage of history between these two elite 135-pounders. Dvalishvili absolutely dominated their first meeting , while Yan answered with a gritty performance in their rematch that left "The Machine" battered and bloodied .
 Now, with their trilogy fight finally about to kickoff, both men have a chance to settle their score once and for all.
 Beyond bragging rights, the stakes are enormous for UFC's Bantamweight division. Dvalishvili has built one of the most impressive championship resumes in recent UFC history, while Yan remains one of the most technically-gifted and accomplished fighters at 135 pounds. By the time the final horn sounds, one man's legacy will receive another major boost, while the other's claim to Bantamweight greatness could take a hit.
 Follow along below for live "Yan vs. Dvalishvili 3" results, round-by-round updates and our full fight recap of below:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Round one: 
 Merab, the worthy challenger, was first into the Octagon, circling the Octagon with gusto as he waited for Yan to make the walk. And he did just that, moments later, with his two sons escorting the dynamic Russian striker to the cage. The referee in charge of the five-round championship showdown was Jason Herzog . And after Bruce Buffer's iconic introductions, we were off and punching …
 Merab got the action started with a low kick that nearly took Yan off his feet. Merab, moments later, landed a hard right cross then reached for a single-leg takedown, but Yan was able to spin out. Undeterred, Merab was back on another takedown, circled around Yan's back, but the Russian was able to remain upright. Merab continued his insane pressure, snatching another leg and getting Yan on a knee, bit once again, he was able to escape. Merab continued to just throw feints and punches like crazy, and Yan finally whiffed with a left cross. Overhand right from Merab, which Yan ducked, and then defended another high crotch takedown. With just 90 seconds to go in the round, Yan had thrown just six strikes! Merab was finally able to takedown Yan, but he was back to his feet quickly, only to get taken to the mat moments later. He was able to get on all fours, with Merab riding him until the horn blared. Domination early from the former champion.
 Round two: 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Merab was still as energetic as ever between rounds, with Yan needing to get going before he falls too far behind. He landed a nice right hand to start the second stanza, then another combination, with Merab countering with a hard shot. Then, just one minute off the clock, he had Yan wrapped up again. Yan got up, only to be dumped back to the canvas. Yan was actually able to reverse on the ground and land a few solid shots as Merab returned to his feet. Merab went for yet another takedown, he was relentless — 13 takedown attempts in six minutes! Merab was able to get behind Yan and dumped him to the canvas along the cage. Yan was able to escape, again, but the Russian was just in full shelled defensive mode through 1.5 rounds. Nice combination from Yan with 90 seconds remaining in the round, with Merab landing a nice overhand right. Yan was able to respond with a nice left hand, but he dumped Yan on the canvas yet again, drilling him with a knee to the mid-section on his way up. Yan tried to corner him along the cage, but Merab was just too much through 10 minutes. Another round in the bank for Merab.
 Round three: 
 Merab with a nice right hand to start round three, while Yan seemed a bit gassed. Yan chased Merab around the cage early, but all that got him was wrapped up in another Georgian pretzel along the cage. Merab with a nice knee on the break, racking up a crazy 20 takedown attempts. Yan with a hard left kick to Merab's gut, defending a takedwon in the center of the cage … two straight. Merab has 50 significant strikes landed, so it was not just all takedowns. Yan continued to chase Merab around the cage, not having much success, but definitely doing better in the takedown defense department. Yan landed a hard shot upstairs, his best punch of the fight, but Merab didn't even flinch. Yan once again tried to trap him along the fence, landed another hard liver shot, but Merab just smiled and shot for another takedown. Yan landed his first real combination and had Merab on his bicycle, but Merab, once again, seemed unfazed. Will give that round to Yan?
 Round four: 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Merab has shot 32 takedowns before round four even started — insanity. Merab continued his takedown assault and Yan continued to defend better as the fight endured. Nice jab from Yan, then another, as Merab continued to bait the champion with feints. Nce right hand from Yan, then a hard left hook to the body as Merab seemed to finally be slowing down. Merab really went after the takedown, got around Yan's back, but once again couldn't do much with it. Yan more or less flipped the fight at this point, able to remain upright as Merab's takedowns dwindled — his face starting to show damage. Nice back-and-forth barrage to close the round. Yan definitely got that one, with it seemingly even heading into the fifth and final frame!
